items.title: I ricchi non vogliono schermi nelle scuole dei loro figli
items.summary: Nella Silicon valley, in California, chi sviluppa app e piattaforme paga rette altissime per istituti privati in cui queste tecnologie non entrano. Le scuole più povere, invece, ne dipendono sempre di più Leggi
items.content:
German Gil è un programmatore e passa gran parte del suo tempo davanti a uno schermo. Nel 2015 si è trasferito a San Francisco e da allora ha lavorato per diverse startup e grandi aziende del settore tecnologico, tra cui Netflix e GitHub.

Ma quando è arrivato il momento di scegliere la scuola per la figlia Victoria, Gil voleva che avesse un’esperienza diversa, in un ambiente in cui “una bambina possa semplicemente essere una bambina”.

Gil e la moglie hanno iscritto Victoria alla Waldorf, un istituto privato basato sulla pedagogia steineriana , che punta molto sul gioco a contatto con la natura. Oggi Victoria fa la quarta elementare e trascorre le ore a scuola lontana dagli schermi. Invece di studiare sui computer portatili Chromebook , nella sua classe si rilegano libri a mano.

Tutto questo, però, ha un costo piuttosto alto. La retta della Waldorf, che si trova nel ricco quartiere di Pacific Heights, ad appena tre chilometri dagli uffici del gigante dell’intelligenza artificiale (ia) Anthropic, è di quarantamila dollari all’anno per la classe dai cinque ai sei anni. Per le superiori si sale a sessantamila. Eppure, nonostante i prezzi, l’approccio dell’istituto è sempre più in voga.

Per quanto possa sembrare controintuitivo, negli ultimi anni molti lavoratori ben pagati della Silicon valley hanno speso cifre enormi per allontanare i loro figli dalle stesse piattaforme che contribuiscono a sviluppare. Le domande d’iscrizione alla Waldorf sono cresciute senza sosta. La direttrice, Lauren Smith, dice che buona parte dei genitori degli alunni della Waldorf lavora nel campo della tecnologia.

Nelle enclave tecnologiche della California, da Mountain View a San Mateo, i genitori vorrebbero che le scuole pubbliche, dove gli schermi in classe sono una presenza fissa, tornassero a concentrarsi sui rapporti umani, seguendo l’esempio della Waldorf. Le loro iniziative hanno spinto alcuni istituti a vietare l’uso degli smartphone e a ridurre i compiti e i test da fare usando il computer.

Mentre si moltiplicano le prove dei danni che i social media e le piattaforme online causano alla crescita (anche i tribunali hanno cominciato a intervenire ), le famiglie e i governi locali stanno rivalutando il rapporto tra i ragazzi e la tecnologia, riflettendo sul ruolo dei dispositivi nell’apprendimento.

Di recente diversi grandi distretti scolastici, come quelli di New York City e Los Angeles, hanno deciso di limitare il ricorso alla tecnologia. Anche in altri paesi del mondo i genitori sono più critici nei confronti dell’uso dei dispositivi.

“Oggi si parla molto di più di questi argomenti rispetto a qualche anno fa”, conferma David Monahan, direttore delle campagne di Fairplay, un’organizzazione statunitense che si batte per limitare l’uso degli schermi tra bambini e bambine.

I genitori della Silicon valley offrono qualcosa in più rispetto ad altre comunità: la conoscenza diretta del settore. Quando l’anno scorso il distretto che riunisce le superiori di San Mateo ha creato una squadra per valutare che conseguenze può avere l’uso dell’ia in classe, almeno due dei componenti lavoravano per grandi aziende tecnologiche, tra cui la sezione di Google che si occupa proprio d’ia, come ha confermato Jennifer Jacobson del consiglio scolastico.

“Rispetto ad altri, questi adulti conoscono meglio la tecnologia”, sottolinea Jacobson. “Sono in grado di prevederne gli sviluppi e il potenziale effetto sull’apprendimento”.

Molte famiglie statunitensi sono sbalordite quando scoprono il modo in cui gli schermi entrano nelle scuole. Jillian Kolongowski, scrittrice che vive a San Mateo, è rimasta senza parole vedendo la figlia di cinque anni tornare a casa con un Chromebook per fare gli esercizi di matematica. “Mi sono detta: ‘Che diavolo è quello? Va all’asilo!’”, racconta Kolongowski.

Candice Wei, una tutor di Palo Alto che aiuta ragazzi e ragazze delle superiori nell’ammissione al college, ha avuto una reazione simile quando ha scoperto che alla scuola dell’infanzia di suo figlio bambine e bambini usavano gli schermi in classe con restrizioni minime. Wei ha così deciso di capire quali fossero le regole applicate alle superiori. “YouTube non è vietato, così come l’ia generativa. È una scelta quasi criminale”, accusa. “Io non permetto che si usino a casa mia. Perché a scuola sì?”.

All’inizio il ricorso alla tecnologia nelle scuole era visto come il segno di un futuro digitale più giusto e accessibile. In molti casi i dispositivi elettronici, essenziali durante la pandemia per garantire le lezioni a distanza, non sono stati abbandonati dopo il ritorno in classe. Nel 2025 il 99 per cento degli insegnanti che avevano partecipato a un sondaggio del New York Times riferiva che i loro studenti avevano ricevuto dispositivi direttamente dalle scuole, mentre l’81 per cento riferiva che i bambini entravano in contatto con gli schermi già a cinque anni.

Oggi gli esperti e un numero crescente di genitori temono l’onnipresenza della tecnologia. Metà degli adolescenti statunitensi trascorre almeno quattro ore al giorno davanti a uno schermo, senza contare il tempo in cui usa i dispositivi per le attività scolastiche. Monahan pensa che la presenza degli schermi in classe non faccia altro che rafforzare queste tendenze. “Che tipo di abitudini promuoviamo a scuola, se ragazzi e ragazze passano ore a fissare gli schermi con l’approvazione dei loro insegnanti?”, si domanda.

Diverse ricerche mostrano che gli studenti memorizzano meglio usando carta e penna invece che uno schermo. Altri sottolineano che l’uso eccessivo dei dispositivi ostacola il legame tra studente e insegnante, un aspetto fondamentale per la crescita emotiva. Inoltre, elimina quello sforzo che favorisce l’apprendimento.

“Le persone sono molto più propense a impegnarsi per un insegnante o un genitore che per un computer, che non ricambierà mai il loro affetto”, spiega Yvonne Kao, dell’organizzazione WestEd, specializzata in istruzione.

Kao nota che negli Stati Uniti l’uso della tecnologia cambia molto tra i diversi distretti scolastici. E racconta di aver sentito parlare di aree rurali in cui non c’è personale in grado di valutare correttamente le diverse tecnologie e abbastanza aggiornato da capire cosa conviene comprare.

I genitori della Silicon valley sono in una posizione diversa. “Hanno una dimestichezza che, credo, si acquisisce solo vivendo immersi in quell’ambiente”, aggiunge Kao. “Sanno cos’è utile e cos’è dannoso, quindi possono provare a trovare un giusto equilibrio”.

La diffusione degli schermi nelle scuole pubbliche ha spinto molte famiglie tra le braccia degli istituti privati. Libere dalla burocrazia locale e statale, le scuole private della California possono cambiare strada più velocemente e introdurre limiti, oltre ad avere più risorse per pagare gli insegnanti invece di affidarsi alle app.

Wei ha aperto la sede locale dell’organizzazione Schools beyond screens ed è convinta che il ricorso agli schermi in classe sia uno dei principali motivi per cui i genitori decidono di abbandonare la scuola pubblica. “Sono stata contattata da persone che hanno preso in considerazione una scuola pubblica per i loro figli, l’hanno visitata, hanno visto studenti incollati agli schermi e hanno pensato: ‘Beh, meglio andare nelle private’”, racconta.

Questa situazione ha spinto Wei e altri a fare pressione sui distretti scolastici perché verifichino le credenziali delle aziende che ottengono appalti milionari con le scuole ed esigano prove solide sulla capacità dei loro prodotti di migliorare l’apprendimento. “Significa chiedere dati precisi sui risultati che si aspettano di ottenere, e sapere qual è il piano nel caso in cui non li raggiungano”, dice Kolongowski, il cui marito lavora nel campo dell’intelligenza artificiale. “Molte aziende del settore pubblicizzano soluzioni davvero allettanti, ma poi i risultati non sono all’altezza delle aspettative”.

Grazie alle pressioni delle famiglie, le scuole pubbliche di San Mateo hanno smesso di distribuire portatili ai bambini fino alla seconda elementare. Gli studenti delle superiori, invece, hanno il divieto assoluto di usare i telefoni. A Mountain View le scuole stanno smettendo di usare i-Ready, una piattaforma per la lettura e lo studio della matematica usata nei distretti scolastici californiani, criticata per le lezioni ripetitive e accusata di condividere i dati personali degli studenti senza il loro consenso.

Intanto le scuole pubbliche di Palo Alto hanno vietato l’uso di un prodotto tecnologico creato a pochi chilometri di distanza: gli occhiali smart .

I sostenitori dell’apprendimento centrato sulla persona sono soddisfatti di questi progressi, ma temono che i distretti con meno risorse rimangano indietro, e siano costretti a usare gli strumenti tecnologici che le scuole più ricche stanno abbandonando.

L’ostilità nei confronti della tecnologia in classe è un fenomeno molto diffuso, sottolinea Jon Valant, direttore del centro di ricerca sulle politiche scolastiche della Brookings institution. A prescindere dal reddito, i genitori vogliono la stessa cosa per i figli: un’istruzione di alta qualità e basata sui rapporti umani. La differenza è che alcuni possono permettersela, mentre altri no.

items.title: Quanto conta il voto dei palestinesi di Israele
items.summary: Dopo le elezioni i partiti arabi sono diventati centrali nel panorama politico israeliano. Ma potranno davvero determinare la formazione del prossimo governo? Leggi
items.content:
Uno dei risultati più importanti delle elezioni che si sono svolte in Israele il 27 ottobre è stata la partecipazione dei cittadini palestinesi. La loro affluenza record alle urne – pari all’80 per cento, contro il 53 per cento della tornata precedente – ha assicurato ai partiti arabi 19 seggi in parlamento, rendendoli un elemento fondamentale della scena politica del paese. Al blocco di opposizione guidato da Gadi Eisenkot basterebbe allearsi con loro per raggiungere la maggioranza e formare un governo che allontanerebbe finalmente Benjamin Netanyahu dal potere dopo quasi vent’anni. Peccato però che questa opzione per il momento resti categoricamente esclusa.

Il successo elettorale palestinese sta quindi mettendo in evidenza quella che l’analista politico Abed Abou Shhadeh su Al Jazeera chiama “una scomoda verità”: cosa succede quando dei cittadini che sono informalmente emarginati sulla scena politica ma il cui voto ha formalmente lo stesso peso diventano abbastanza potenti da decidere chi governa? Secondo Abou Shhadeh i palestinesi di Israele si trovano di fronte a una questione fondamentale: “Possono davvero determinare l’esito politico e, se sì, questo li rende cittadini alla pari?”.

Come ricostruisce Abou Shhadeh nel suo articolo, per i palestinesi cittadini di Israele da tempo il voto è un dilemma: “Se non si mobilitano per andare a votare, il rischio che la destra ebraica prenda il potere è elevato. Se invece votano, non c’è alcuna garanzia che la loro partecipazione si traduca in politiche che proteggano o avvantaggino le loro comunità”. Storicamente le comunità arabe di Israele hanno riposto scarsa fiducia nelle elezioni e in alcuni periodi, per esempio durante la seconda intifada, la loro affluenza alle urne è stata molto bassa. Anche perché il regime militare, l’occupazione e la repressione imposte da Israele hanno a lungo limitato la loro capacità di organizzarsi e partecipare alla vita politica.

I palestinesi cittadini di Israele, noti anche come arabi israeliani, sono i discendenti degli abitanti della Palestina rimasti all’interno dei confini di Israele dopo la creazione dello stato nel 1948. Allora erano 150mila; oggi sono diventati circa due milioni e sono un quinto della popolazione del paese. Tra il 1948 e il 1966 hanno vissuto sotto un’amministrazione militare che imponeva solo a loro limitazioni di movimento, coprifuoco e restrizioni all’attività politica. Già allora e poi nei decenni successivi sono stati oggetto di leggi e politiche discriminatorie adottate dai vari governi israeliani, racconta un approfondimento di Middle East Eye .

Secondo Adalah, un centro legale con sede a Haifa, più di 65 leggi approvate in Israele dal 1948 discriminano i palestinesi in modo esplicito o implicito. Riguardano soprattutto la proprietà terriera, l’alloggio, i finanziamenti pubblici e il ricongiungimento familiare. Uno dei primi esempi è stata la legge sulla proprietà degli assenti del 1950, che classificava come “assenti” i palestinesi fuggiti o cacciati dalle loro case durante la Nakba, la catastrofe del 1948, e poneva tutti i loro beni sotto il controllo dello stato. Ne sono seguite molte altre fino ad arrivare all’adozione, nel 2018, della legge che definisce Israele come “stato nazione del popolo ebraico”, declassa l’arabo da lingua ufficiale a lingua con uno “status speciale” e indica lo sviluppo degli insediamenti ebraici come un interesse nazionale.

Oggi i palestinesi vivono soprattutto in città e villaggi in Galilea, nel nord del paese, nella zona nota come Triangolo, nel centro, e nel deserto del Naqab (o Negev), nel sud. Circa l’80 per cento di loro è musulmano, il 10 per cento cristiano e altrettanti sono drusi. Nelle città in cui abitano la qualità della vita è inferiore rispetto a quelle a maggioranza ebraica. Le disuguaglianze riguardano soprattutto le abitazioni, i servizi pubblici e le infrastrutture. Inoltre si registra un livello più alto di criminalità e violenza, acuito da un’inadeguata protezione delle forze dell’ordine.

Secondo l’ong Abraham initiatives, il 50 per cento dei crimini violenti avvenuti in Israele ha coinvolto dei palestinesi. Negli ultimi anni il bilancio delle vittime è cresciuto da 116 nel 2022 a 244 nel 2023 fino a 252 nel 2025. L’organizzazione lega questa crisi a “una presenza ridotta delle forze dell’ordine e ai rapporti tesi con la polizia israeliana”. Anche le indagini ne risentono: la polizia israeliana ha risolto meno del 15 per cento dei casi di omicidio che riguardano i palestinesi, rispetto a un tasso del 65 per cento quando le vittime sono ebree.

Dopo gli attacchi di Hamas del 7 ottobre 2023 lo spazio di libertà per i palestinesi cittadini di Israele si è ridotto ulteriormente. Commenti sui social media contrari alla guerra di Israele a Gaza hanno scatenato arresti, licenziamenti, sospensioni e indagini disciplinari. La paura aleggia tra gli studenti palestinesi delle università del paese, mentre le politiche di estrema destra attuate dal governo di Netanyahu negli ultimi quattro anni hanno inasprito il clima nei confronti della comunità palestinese di Israele. In vista delle elezioni le cose sono peggiorate e un’analisi condotta dal sito di informazione Arabic post su più di 10mila messaggi sui social media relativi al voto ha rilevato che il 40 per cento di quelli pubblicati dai candidati della fazione di Netanyahu riguardava arabi o palestinesi, e il 94 per cento di questi era di natura ostile.

Per tutti questi motivi i palestinesi di Israele si sono organizzati e sono andati a votare in massa. Come commenta Abou Shhadeh su Al Jazeera, “hanno corso un rischio prendendo sul serio la loro cittadinanza e rivendicando il diritto alla piena uguaglianza politica e a un ruolo significativo nel plasmare il futuro del paese”. Molti di loro ora temono che il successo politico possa tradursi in nuove intimidazioni, violenza e repressione. Vari politici vicini a Netanyahu hanno già accusato gli arabi di aver “rubato le elezioni”, mentre il vicepresidente della knesset Moshe Feiglin è arrivato a dire che la mobilitazione elettorale dei palestinesi è stata “il 7 ottobre” della politica israeliana.

items.title: Il freddo aiuta a perdere peso?
items.summary: Il freddo aiuta a perdere peso?
items.content:
Il freddo aiuta a perdere peso? Sì, ma perché accada non basta fare la doccia fredda: occorre un'esposizione regolare e prolungata alle basse temperature. Ricercatori delle Università di Nottingham (Inghilterra) e del Centro Medico dell'Università di Leida (Paesi Bassi) hanno reclutato un gruppo di 47 adulti con obesità e assegnato alla metà di loro un gilet e una cintura refrigeranti, mantenuti a una temperatura di 15 °C..
I malcapitati hanno dovuto indossarli due ore al giorno per 6 settimane, portandoli come se nulla fosse sopra una maglietta sottile durante le normali attività quotidiane.
. Grasso bruno
Risultato: i volontari hanno perso in media 0,9 kg, quasi tutti di grasso corporeo, contro gli zero kg persi (e i 6 etti guadagnati) del gruppo di controllo. L'ipotesi è che questa fonte di freddo costante, poco costosa e facilmente integrabile nella routine di ogni giorno, attivi il tessuto adiposo bruno, che brucia le scorte di grasso corporeo per produrre calore.. Questo meccanismo è benefico per il metabolismo dei grassi e del glucosio, e riduce i livelli di infiammazione dell'organismo..

items.summary: Article URL: https://pwn.college/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50387796 Points: 145 # Comments: 19
items.content: You have entered the pwn.college DOJO, an education platform for learners to develop and practice core cybersecurity skills in a hands-on fashion. Entering, you receive your "white belt" , signifying the beginning of your hacker life. From here, you will learn cybersecurity by diving deep into the core of computing, using that journey to absorb cybersecurity concepts. This will involve melding your mind to your terminal, whispering instructions to the CPU, and strumming bits directly onto networks. That terminal cursor blinking above? It will be your stalwart companion through this adventure as you practice, earn your belts , and, eventually, make perfect. Every dojo has its sensei. This platform is maintained by an awesome team of hackers at Arizona State University. It powers much of ASU's cybersecurity curriculum, and is open, for free, to participation for interested people around the world! Enjoy your journey! If you have questions, comments, suggestions, and feedback, please join our Discord server or email us at [email protected] ! items.title: Nvidia Kubernetes Engine (NVKE)
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/nvke Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50387738 Points: 74 # Comments: 19
items.content:
Run a managed Kubernetes service on your own NVIDIA GPU infrastructure. NVIDIA Kubernetes® Engine (NVKE) provides the management plane that platform teams install to create and operate Kubernetes clusters for their customers. Each workload cluster has its own Kubernetes control plane, etcd and node pools. You operate the NVKE management plane; your customers use their clusters through the Kubernetes API and kubectl .

Preview: NVKE is available as a preview. APIs, configuration and behavior can change between releases, and we do not recommend NVKE for production workloads. See Preview status and known limitations .

The local quickstart runs on a Linux host or VM, amd64 or arm64 , with at least 6 CPUs, 12 GiB of free memory and 100 GiB of free disk . It requires Docker, virtual TPM support and the tools listed in the guide. Follow its setup through workload-cluster creation and confirm the cluster's nodes report Ready . On macOS, use the local site guide , which runs the evaluation inside a Colima virtual machine.

For a real installation, you supply the machines, networking, node images and registries, and configure access to NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo) . NICo is the sole compatible infrastructure provider at preview. The platform and version reference lists validated combinations and pinned dependencies.

The preview needs explicit operator configuration: API authentication is off and the API uses plain HTTP after installation. Configure API authentication and protected access before admitting callers. The management cluster does not upgrade, scale or replace itself, and there is no management-plane upgrade or backup/restore procedure. FDE node images are for evaluation and provide no data-at-rest confidentiality. Read the known limitations before choosing an evaluation or installation path.

The diagram shows the NVKE product family, how it sits on NICo and your GPU machines, and which components talk to each other.

NVKE is not a Kubernetes distribution and not a Cluster API flavour. It is a self-hosting factory for Kubernetes clusters : a throwaway seed cluster stands up a management cluster, and the management plane on it then provisions and lifecycle-manages many isolated workload clusters on demand.

Read What is NVKE for the operator workflow and Architecture for the implementation and data flows.

Use Go 1.27.3 , the version pinned in go.work , and GNU Make 4 or later . Public Go modules must be reachable on the first build. Flox is optional and supplies the repository's development tools; on macOS, it also supplies GNU Make 4. See Development for toolchain setup.

This builds the workspace and writes nine binaries to bin/ : agent , updater , controller , nvkectl , capd-reboot-controller , nvke-os-image-check , management-engine , tenant-api and operator-api . Building does not start a management plane or create a cluster. The node agent runs on Linux.

The workspace guide explains the modules and outputs. For local services and test environments, see Local development setup . Before submitting a change, follow CONTRIBUTING.md and run make preflight ; it selects checks for the modules you changed.

The documentation index links the remaining guides and references.

Contributions, bug reports and documentation improvements are welcome. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md ; open an issue before substantial work so maintainers can agree on the approach.

items.title: White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses
items.summary: US media reports there are calls to replace Pete Hegseth, who also faces a possible impeachment vote, while Marco Rubio is rumoured to be eyeing a presidential run.
items.content:
The White House has denied rumours that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio might leave their jobs in a post-election shakeup of the Trump administration.

US media have reported there are calls to replace Hegseth - in particular over his handling of the Iran war, which is being blamed for heavy Republican election losses.

One outgoing congressional Republican has threatened to force an impeachment vote against Hegseth as early as next week. The defence secretary posted a video statement defending his record and denouncing the effort.

"You see, they attack me. They attack us because we are effective," he said. "It's not going to work. We will not back down."

Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war

Meanwhile, Rubio is denying reports he is considering leaving his post ahead of a 2028 presidential run.

Working for Trump until the end of his term has "always been my plan," Rubio told The New York Times in an interview.

"I love the work I'm doing," Rubio said. "And plus I always laugh when they say he's going to leave his job. I go, 'Which one?'"

The White House and US State Department also shut down reports that Rubio might be leaving after this week's midterm losses, with both calling it "fake news".

The defence secretary, though, faces a more uncertain political future.

Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have both blamed the Iran war for Republican losses that allowed Democrats full control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

In a telephone interview with ABC News, Trump said that he had received "calls about" Hegseth, but added that he had "every intention" of keeping him.

Later on Thursday, he told reporters at the White House that "Pete Hegseth has done a fantastic job", and went on to list what he sees are some of his achievements, including the arrest of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro in January and the Iran war, now into its ninth month.

ZURCHER: Midterm carnage weakens Trump but he still wields power for now

ANALYSIS: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war

The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Trump might be, however, considering ousting General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Centcom chief Admiral Brad Cooper. Both played significant roles in offering guidance on the war, which started eight months ago.

Meanwhile, Republican Representative Thomas Massie, a frequent critic of Trump, has said he will push ahead with plans to push for Hegseth's impeachment.

He told news site Politico that he will trigger his resolution to impeach the defence secretary early next week.

And on X, he warned that the president should replace Hegseth before a new Democratic-controlled Congress forms in January.

"He should do it while he can still get the replacements confirmed in the Senate," Massie wrote on X.

Hegseth has also been rumoured to be interested in running for an open Tennessee Senate seat.

In his video statement, Hegseth denounced the "sham articles of impeachment" effort against him from a "disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies", and listed ways the department has fulfilled Trump's America First agenda under his leadership.

That includes, he said, reviving military recruitment, rebuilding the defence industrial base, and rooting out diversity initiatives.

Of the Democrats, he said: "Their policies don't work. So their obsession with political theatre disguised as power drives them to try to destroy their opponents. It's all about the politics of personal destruction."

Vance says Republicans lost big because of Iran war: 'Everyone knows why we lost'

Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here . Those outside the UK can sign up here .

items.title: Le Borse oggi, 6 novembre. Continua il crollo per le vendite sul tech: male l’Asia, Milano in rosso
items.summary: Tonfo degli indici coreani e giapponesi per i timori che i cambiamenti negli Usa possano colpire gli investimenti chiave nell'intelligenza artificiale
items.content:
ROMA – Prosegue il tonfo delle Borse dopo il crollo di Wall Street di ieri . Il timore degli investitori è che il risultato delle midterm negli Usa possa ridurre e bloccare gli investimenti nell’intelligenza artificiale e ostacolare la realizzazione di nuovi data center. A pagare sono stati principalmente i titoli tech , e infatti l’Asia ha chiuso con perdite elevate: il Nikkei ha lasciato quasi il 6% toccando i minimi da aprile. In Europa Piazza Affari parte male, ma sono tutte le piazze a subire cali.

Borse asiatiche, ancora una chiusura negativa a Tokyo e Seul

A quasi metà mattinata il prezzo del gas continua a scendere. Al Ttf di Amsterdam i future sono trattati a 87,56 euro al megawattora, con una flessione del 3,46%.

Piazza Affari nei primi scambi riduce di qualche frazione l'avvio ampiamente negativo: l'indice Ftse Mib cede l'1% in linea con la Borsa di Parigi, mentre Londra e Francoforte cedono circa un punto percentuale e mezzo. Lo spread Btp-Bund è calmo a quota 108 punti base, con l'euro fiacco (-0,2%) contro il dollaro quota 1,118. Nel settore energia, dopo una partenza in rialzo, il gas scende del 2% a 88,4 euro al Megawattora, mentre il petrolio a New York perde qualche frazione di punto a 90 dollari al barile. In un clima nervoso, con i future sull'avvio di Wall street incerti, in Piazza Affari tra i titoli maggiori il più pesante è Saipem, che cede il 2,7%, seguito da Banco Bpm in ribasso del 2,6%. Generalmente negativo il settore del credito, con Mps che oscilla sulla parità dopo i conti del trimestre. Rimbalza Technoprobe (+1,7%), in rialzo dell'1,8% Buzzi.

Improvvisa inversione di rotta per il prezzo del gas. Dopo un'apertura in rialzo, attualmente i future al Ttf di Amterdam stanno perdendo l'1,23% e vengono trattati a 89,35 euro al megawattora.

La Borsa di Milano apre in deciso calo con il Ftse Mib che cede l'1,58% a quota 49.710 punti. A trascinare giù il listino è il comparto del credito con Banco Bpm che cede il 2,88% dopo i conti e Intesa il 2,25%. Bper -2,16%. Banca Mps -0,83% ha chiuso i nove mesi con un utile netto di 1,657 miliardi di euro, in crescita del 21,2% su base annua. Maglia nera per Enel -4,28%.

Le Borse europee aprono l'ultima seduta della settimana in forte calo, sulla scia del profondo rosso a Wall Street e sui listini asiatici dopo il crollo del comparto tech e IA sui timori che la vittoria elettorale dei Democratici possa portare a una regolamentazione più severa dell'intelligenza artificiale. Nei primi scambi a Londra l'indice Ftse cede l'1,45% a 10.626,41 punti, a Francoforte il Dax l'1,74% a 25.872 punti e a Parigi il Cac40 perde l'1,4% a 8.089,77 punti.

Mare Group, società di ingegneria ad alta tecnologia quotata in Borsa su Euronext Growth Milan, ha sottoscritto un accordo vincolante per l'acquisizione del 51% di Proser, società specializzata nella progettazione, produzione e assistenza di apparati elettronici ed elettromeccanici per i settori Aerospace & Defence. Lo rende noto un comunicato dell'acquirente, con un corrispettivo di circa 1,6 milioni di euro e closing atteso entro il 31 dicembre prossimo, prevede inoltre opzioni di acquisto e di vendita sul restante 49% del capitale, esercitabili a partire dal primo maggio 2030, che disciplinano il possibile passaggio a Mare Group dell'intera partecipazione in Proser.

Borse asiatiche, ancora una chiusura negativa a Tokyo e Seul

Mercati azionari asiatici e dell'area del Pacifico tutti in calo sulla scia dello scivolone di Wall Street e dei i timori legati ai risultati delle elezioni statunitensi, che tra l'altro potrebbero rallentare gli investimenti nei data center dedicati all'intelligenza artificiale. I listini più pesanti sono Seul che ha ceduto il 6% netto e Tokyo in calo del 5,9%. Negative anche le Borse cinesi, con Shenzhen che ha perso il 2,2% e Shanghai l'1,1%. In calo del'1,2% Hong Kong, mentre Sidney ha contenuto il ribasso di mezzo punto percentuale.

Come il petrolio, anche il gas segna un aumento di prezzo questa mattina. Al Ttf di Amsterdam i future sono trattati a 92,17 euro al megawattora, con un rialzo dell'1,65%.

Borsee europee, attesa apertura in calo per Milano dopo crollo di ieri

Borse europee attese in calo all'apertura di questa mattina, sulla scia della giornata nera di Wall Street, affossata dal crollo dei titolo tecnologici, la previsione per il Ftse Mib di Milano è del -1,98%, l'Euro Stoxx 50 è atteso a -1,11%, Francoforte a -0,81%, Parigi a -0,26%, Londra a -0,99%.

Prezzo del petrolio in rialzo questa mattina sui mercati delle materie prime: il Wti con consegna a dicembre passa di mano a 91,71 dollari al barile con un avanzamento dell'1,31% mentre il Brent con consegna a gennaio è scambiato a 100.00 dollari al barile con una crescita dell'1,74%.

Future in ordine sparso a Wall Street dopo la chiusura in profondo rosso di ieri , quando i principali indici hanno subito il peggior calo giornaliero dai tempi delle turbolenze scatenate dai dazi nell'aprile 2025, in un clima di preoccupazione per la possibilità che i Democratici introducano normative più stringenti nel settore dell'intelligenza artificiale. I future sul Dow Jones cedono lo 0,96%, quelli sullo S&P 500 sono sulla parità e i future sul Nasdaq avanzano dello 0,72%.

Trump ha attribuito il crollo del mercato azionario di ieri alla vittoria elettorale dei rivali del Partito democratico nelle elezioni di midterm. “È crollato oggi perché i democratici hanno avuto un grande successo martedì. Che tristezza, la colpa è solo vostra!", ha scritto il presidente Usa su Truth dopo la chiusura dei mercati statunitensi.

Seul peggio di Tokyo, -8,5% e contrattazioni sospese per 20 minuti

L'indice Kospi di Seul è crollato dell'8,5%, attestandosi a 4.923 punti, facendo scattare un meccanismo di sospensione automatica delle contrattazioni per la durata di 20 minuti. La borsa sudcoreana segue il timore che cambiamento nel panorama politico in Usa possa colpire gli investimenti chiave nell'intelligenza artificiale, considerati fondamentali per la crescita economica, e l'apertura nettamente negativa di Tokyo a -5,1%.

Il Nikkei, l'indice di punta della borsa di Tokyo, è caduto di oltre il 5% in apertura dopo il crollo di Wall Street (-5,5% in chiusura), dopo i risultati delle elezioni americane che potrebbero rallentare gli investimenti nei data center dedicati all'intelligenza artificiale. L'indice di riferimento Nikkei è sceso del 5,1% a 56.930 punti nelle prime contrattazioni.

items.title: Democratic socialist defeats incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayor's race
items.summary: The results mean America's two most populous cities - New York and Los Angeles - will be led by democratic socialists.
items.content:
Democratic socialist Nithya Raman has toppled incumbent Karen Bass in the race for mayor of Los Angeles.

Raman's win stunned political watchers in California after she entered the race as a long-shot candidate against Bass, a political heavyweight who previously served in Congress and had never lost a race for political office.

Raman has frequently been compared to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Both are democratic socialists and ran on progressive platforms.

Her win solidifies that America's two biggest cities will now be led by democratic socialists, which include some of the most high-profile politicians in the US, such as Mamdani and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

Los Angeles was always likely to have a Democratic mayor but the question in the city - the second most populous city in the US - was just how left voters would be willing to go.

Bass, also Democrat, announced that she had called and conceded to Raman in a post on social media on Thursday, writing "while this is not the outcome we hoped for, the people of Los Angeles have spoken."

"Moving this city forward is what Los Angeles needs from all of us," Bass wrote. "I love Los Angeles. I believe in Los Angeles. And I will continue to ensure the promise of a better life belongs to all of us."

Boebert, billionaires' tax and other midterms races still to watch

Food, fuel and taxes – can the Democrats actually make life cheaper?

'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat

Raman, a member of city council and Indian immigrant, ran on a platform of change and fixing the "broken status quo and the politicians who failed them over and over again".

She ran on cutting homelessness, increasing housing in the city, saving Hollywood jobs from continued cuts and protecting residents from immigration enforcement efforts. Raman also vowed to fix the city's many issues, including helping beautification efforts, fixing roads and even helping bring back nightlife in the city.

The major issue in the race, however, was the LA fires, which killed dozens of people and razed neighbourhoods across the area in 2025. Bass faced intense political fallout over her absence during the emergency and the city's response to the disaster.

The next mayor in LA will oversee hosting the Super Bowl in 2027 and the 2028 Summer Olympics.

Raman entered the race as a long-shot candidate but slowly shored up support, especially from younger voters, before besting reality star Spencer Pratt in the primary race earlier this year.

Raman's win over Bass has all the appearances of echoing voter sentiment across the US as part of sweeping Democratic wins, including in deep-Republican country that hadn't seen liberal leaders in decades.

Washington DC also elected democratic socialist Janeese Lewis George as its new mayor, furthering progressive leadership in another major US city.

US President Donald Trump was asked at the White House about the wins by politicians on the left flank of the Democratic Party and said, "If you go by history, it's going to be a disaster".

Such candidates have become a focal point of attacks by Republicans.

Bass had been a prominent member of Congress before becoming LA's first black female mayor. Her roots are closely tied to LA and its history, even working as a community organiser during the violent 1992 riots over police brutality in the beating of Rodney King, who was black.

ZURCHER: Midterm carnage weakens Trump but he still wields power for now

ANALYSIS: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war

items.title: Samsung Secrets: i Samsung AI TV si trasformano in una console di ultima generazione, serve solo un controller
items.summary: Il Gaming Hub di Samsung nasconde un vero PC da gaming all'interno del televisore. Ecco cosa serve per giocare in 4K a 60 fps (e oltre) direttamente dal cloud ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Quando si pensa di acquistare una nuova console da gioco o un PC per il gaming in 4K, ci sono sempre più ostacoli: hardware introvabile e prezzi fuori controllo. Eppure, se in salotto c’è un televisore Samsung AI TV, quella “console” è già pronta all'uso e non ha bisogno di alcuna “scatola" aggiuntiva posizionata sotto lo schermo. Si chiama Samsung Gaming Hub ed è uno degli elementi più potenti — e spesso meno esplorati — della piattaforma Smart TV Tizen. Non è una semplice raccolta di app, ma un ambiente che trasforma il TV in una stazione da gioco di alto livello, azzerando la necessità di acquistare hardware dedicato.

Il principio alla base del Gaming Hub è semplice: l'elaborazione grafica non avviene sul televisore, ma su server remoti ad altissime prestazioni. Il TV riceve un flusso video a bassissima latenza e invia i comandi impartiti dal controller.

A differenza di qualche anno fa, la maturità delle piattaforme di cloud gaming di oggi garantisce una qualità sovrapponibile a quella di una macchina fisica di altissimo livello , e i Samsung AI TV supportano i migliori servizi oggi disponibili per qualità e titoli disponibili:

Dal Gaming Hub puoi sfogliare direttamente il catalogo aggregato dei titoli disponibili, ricevere raccomandazione dei giochi che ti possono interessare, con indicazione chiara dei servizi di cloud gaming in cui li puoi trovare. Basta selezionare il gioco, la piattaforma e sei pronto a iniziare.

Accedere a centinaia di titoli con il Gaming Hub è più semplice di quello che credi: basta collegare un controller. Il Gaming Hub abbatte qualsiasi barriera perché non richiede un gamepad proprietario : Samsung AI TV supportano infatti i principali controller per console e Bluetooth: c’è la compatibilità nativa via Bluetooth o USB via cavo per i controller Xbox, Xbox Elite, PlayStation DualSense e DualShock 4, Amazon Luna.

Come si collega? Dalla schermata principale del Gaming Hub, basta selezionare l'icona del controller per avviare la ricerca Bluetooth ed effettuare l'abbinamento in pochi secondi. Collegando un cavo USB a una porta del TV o del box One Connect, il riconoscimento è immediato e plug-and-play.

E se sei un amante dei giochi in prima persona e non ami il controller da gioco non c’è nessun problema. Puoi anche collegare mouse e tastiera , sia via Bluetooth che tramite le porte USB, e giocare esattamente come da PC. E siccome anche l’audio è importante, con i Samsung AI TV puoi collegare direttamente anche cuffie e auricolari Bluetooth, con gestione dell'audio a 360° e modalità a bassa latenza.

Se invece possiedi già un PC da gaming rig o una console di ultima generazione (come PS5 o Xbox Series X), il Gaming Hub si trasforma nel centro di controllo per le sorgenti esterne via HDMI 2.1. I Samsung AI TV sono equipaggiati di quattro ingressi HDMI 2.1 completi che offrono accesso a tutte le funzionalità aggiuntive dello standard pensate per il gaming.

Collegando un PC da gaming, i modelli Micro RGB, Neo QLED e OLED Samsung più recenti spingono il refresh rate oltre lo standard dei 120 Hz, raggiungendo perfino i 165 Hz , garantendo la fluidità e l’input lag tipici dei monitor da eSports. Grazie al supporto nativo per VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro e, sulla gamma OLED, alla compatibilità NVIDIA G-Sync, lo schermo del TV adatta in tempo reale la sua frequenza ai framerate del PC o della console, azzerando tearing e micro-scatti per una schermata di gioco sempre incredibilmente fluida.

Grazie alla funzione ALLM (bassa latenza automatica), i Samsung AI TV riconoscono automaticamente la console o il PC e impostano automaticamente la modalità gioco. Grazie all’IA, il TV riconosce il tipo di gioco e ottimizza automaticamente l’immagine per garantire la resa migliore in base al genere. Premendo l'apposito tasto sul telecomando si richiama poi la Game Bar, un menù dedicato che consente di visualizzare in tempo reale il frame e di accedere rapidamente a tutte le funzioni di gioco. Tra le ultime novità troviamo la funzione MiniMap Auto Detect che sfrutta l’intelligenza artificiale per riconoscere la mini mappa di gioco e la ingrandisce in un riquadro dedicato. Il Virtual Aim Point sovrappone invece un mirino virtuale su schermo per aiutarti ad ottenere maggiore precisione negli sparatutto in prima persona.

items.title: MoofTCP – A modern replacement for MacTCP on 68k Macs
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/matthewmrichter/mooftcp Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50386789 Points: 46 # Comments: 20
items.content:
A modern, memory-lean replacement for MacTCP on 68k Macs running System 6.

MoofTCP is a drop-in replacement for Apple's MacTCP. Programs written for MacTCP run on it unchanged, but underneath it is a fresh TCP/IP stack written from scratch in portable C, with its own control panel, installer and DHCP client. It was built for a Mac Classic with 4 MB of RAM, so every byte counts.

MacTCP is wonderful, but it is old, and on a 4 MB Mac Classic with a SCSI Wi-Fi/Ethernet adapter like BlueSCSI it can be slow to answer, hungry for memory, and awkward to set up. MoofTCP aims, in this order, for:

...all while using no more resident memory than MacTCP does .

To go back to MacTCP, run the installer and click Remove . The Read Me file in the release has the details, including how to switch between MoofTCP and MoofTCP Lite.

StuffIt Lite 3.6 is tested as working for expanding the .hqx packages.

Tested on a real Mac Classic (System 6.0.8, 4 MB, BlueSCSI v2 WiFi with DaynaPORT) and in the Snow emulator.

Have a program that doesn't work? Please open an issue (see below).

MultiFinder grows the system heap on demand, so free memory varies more there.

MoofTCP keeps a small diagnostic log in memory. If a program misbehaves but the Mac keeps running, run MoofDiag right away (it is in the release's diagnostic tools download), and open an issue with the MoofDiag.out file it writes next to itself, plus a note about what you were doing. Feel free to ask your LLM to analyze the codebase and the diagnostic output as well and to submit fix PRs.

You only need Docker. The pinned Retro68 cross-compiler image is pulled automatically.

release.sh also needs hfsutils, macutils, unar, gcc and Python 3.

The portable core and the glue logic are tested on your desktop with gcc and CMake (AddressSanitizer and UBSan are on by default):

The emulator tests (Snow) need Apple system software and the BlueSCSI DaynaPORT image. Those are not in this repository and you must supply them yourself; the scripts in scripts/ ( setup-home.sh , golden-stage.sh ) show what is expected.

Bug reports, compatibility reports ("program X does/doesn't work") and pull requests are welcome. For code changes, please read CONTRIBUTING.md and run the host tests first (see above). CLAUDE.md is a detailed map of the code and its rules. Security problems: see SECURITY.md .

MIT . "MacTCP" and "StuffIt" are trademarks of their owners and are used here only to describe compatibility. MoofTCP contains no Apple or third-party code; building it uses Apple's interfaces as shipped in the Retro68 toolchain.

items.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
items.summary: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
items.content:
Pope Leo XIV is beginning a lengthy trip to Latin America just three weeks after surgery for lung cancer - a tour that includes a much-anticipated "homecoming" to Peru where he was a priest for many years.

The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition".

It was Leo himself who revealed last month that doctors had discovered a tumour during a routine scan. The growth was removed along with the lower lobe of his right lung and his medical team then confirmed the cancer had not spread.

At a briefing in Rome ahead of the trip, which takes in Uruguay and Argentina as well as Peru, a spokeswoman stressed that Pope Leo had "fantastic stamina" and was "extremely enthusiastic" about the schedule which he had "personally confirmed... with no changes".

"The Vatican's message with this trip is, 'that was a short episode and now we're back on track'," Professor Massimo Faggioli of Villanova University told the BBC, pointing out that the Pope has had a busy return to work since his surgery.

"We have seen him in these last few days making speeches, audiences and so on. He seems in great shape. That was important."

The 12-day tour would be demanding for anyone, though. It incorporates multiple long-haul and local flights and covers thousands of miles from the Amazon to the Andes.

The starting point will be Uruguay, where the number of Catholics has fallen away steeply in recent years and which is getting its first Papal visit in four decades.

Leo then heads for Argentina, homeland of Pope Francis, his predecessor.

"This visit is also a homage to Francis, who didn't make it to Argentina [as pope]," says Father Fernando Laguna, the rector of Santa Maria Addolorata, Argentina's national church in Rome.

"When this visit by Pope Leo was announced, it filled all of our hearts with joy," he told the BBC. "I always thought he would go, despite his illness. I don't think he ever thought of calling it off!"

The priest is installing a big screen inside the church in Rome to allow parishioners to follow all the key moments of the trip from afar. The building is already decked out with posters declaring Pope Leo is welcome in Argentina. "We're waiting for you!", one proclaims.

This leg of the Pope's journey - which includes meetings with heads of state as well as religious events - could be the most politically sensitive. President Javier Milei once called Pope Francis "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor. In turn, Argentina's bishops have criticised Milei's harsh austerity measures, making sweeping cuts to social spending.

But Milei has already welcomed Pope Leo, writing in a post on X that Argentina awaits "with immense joy". Millions are expected to turn out to greet him.

The highlight of the trip is undoubtedly saved for last, when Pope Leo reaches Peru - described by the Vatican as a return to his roots.

Born in the US, the then Robert Prevost spent almost 20 years in Peru, on and off, and even has Peruvian citizenship. That time is seen as fundamental to shaping his papacy.

His schedule includes a return to the diocese of Chiclayo where he was ordained bishop in 2014 and remained until Francis moved him to the Vatican almost a decade later.

He will also travel to Cusco, former capital of the Inca Empire, to say Mass more than 3,000m above sea level before heading to Pucallpa in the Amazon.

In all three countries, the Vatican says the Pope will have meetings with survivors of clerical sexual abuse - an issue which clouded a 2018 visit to Chile and Peru by his predecessor.

"This is how the papacy reconnects with Latin America after Francis, whose visits to the region were not always seamless," is how Professor Faggioli sees it.

He believes Pope Leo has a strong sense of the unity of the Americas as one continent. "Democracies are in trouble there, so there are so many things he can address," he suggests.

"The big question then is the United States. There's no question he wants to go. So will he travel when [President Donald] Trump is still in office? I'm sure they're thinking about this."

items.title: Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Article URL: https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50386338 Points: 195 # Comments: 67
items.content:
Today we are introducing our second model generation with Inkling 2 Small. It is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, and supports image inputs and variable effort.

Inkling 2 Small far surpasses our previous models’ scores on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 31, reflecting gains in performance on agentic coding, vision, knowledge work, and reasoning. The increase in capabilities comes from improvements made at every step of our training process, including more efficient pre-training and a large, unified RL run.

Inkling 2 Small will initially be available through Tinker, with closed weights, following the approach we outlined in a safe path to open weights . We intend to make the full weights available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.

You can try Inkling 2 Small on Tinker Playground today. The model is also available for fine-tuning and sampling on Tinker; checkpoints will be downloadable with the release of Inkling 2 Small’s weights.

Inkling 2 Small is more capable across the board than our first generation, particularly in long-horizon autonomous work.

Inkling 2 Small’s vision and agentic capabilities enable it to incorporate visual feedback to iteratively build and refine websites, games, and 3D designs with interactive elements.

Inkling 2 Small was trained with RL on hundreds of thousands of long-horizon coding tasks across multiple agent harnesses and context-compaction strategies. We increased the quality of our synthetic coding data pipeline and moved beyond unit-test rewards alone; many tasks included an agentic RL grader that evaluated how the model approached the problem, not just whether its code passed. We also tested early checkpoints of Inkling 2 Small on OpenCode under the name Fledge-Alpha to assess our model’s performance on coding tasks in the real world.

The result is a model that is both stronger at coding and easier to use inside real agent loops. Inkling 2 Small improves on usability compared to Inkling: it follows instructions better, considers changes carefully, and verifies its work without being asked.

Beyond conventional software tasks, Inkling 2 Small was also trained on long-horizon autoresearch tasks. This included agentic GPU kernel optimization and ML tasks such as post-training a model autonomously, all run across a range of GPU architectures.

To demonstrate its end-to-end autoresearch performance, we tested Inkling 2 Small on a task Proximal built for one of our internal benchmarks. Inkling 2 Small autonomously trained Qwen3.5-4B on Tinker to predict various time series such as weather and Wikipedia page views. It started by analyzing the tasks and writing its own evaluator, experimented with training datasets and recipes, and tried various approaches to SFT and RL, while debugging the process as it goes. After 4.5 hours of work and $426 in Tinker spend, the trained model has more than doubled its forecasting score.

Inkling 2 Small processes image inputs using a 292M-parameter vision encoder based on Perception Encoder Bolya et al., 2025 . . We use 20×20-pixel patches with 2×2 spatial pooling, and interleave image patches with text tokens. The model demonstrates strong visual capabilities across multiple categories, including OCR, grounding, infographic interpretation, and visual reasoning.

The model uses vision in the loop to interpret and validate the visual coding output it generates. Pending the release of its weights, it is set to be the top open-weights model on DesignArena .

items.title: Delhi's toxic winter air is back - is the Indian capital prepared for pollution?
items.summary: The Delhi government has announced a four-month winter action plan, but experts say that won't be enough.
items.content:
There are two cardboard boxes in Meenu Rana's living room in Delhi. One is filled with Diwali decorations and twinkling lights. The other holds air purifiers.

"The mornings have already started feeling stuffy. It will get worse in the coming days, so it's better to be prepared," says the 43-year-old teacher.

She is not alone. Every year, as winter and the festive season approach, residents of India's capital begin preparing for something far less celebratory: months of breathing polluted air.

Delhi and its satellite cities record some of the world's highest pollution levels through the year. But as winter sets in, the air often becomes unbearable.

Falling temperatures and slower winds trap pollutants close to the ground instead of allowing them to disperse. Smoke from crop residue burning in neighbouring states adds to emissions from vehicles and factories, as well as construction dust. Firecrackers used during festivals often worsen air quality.

The result is noxious air and a familiar question: why does pollution return year after year, and why hasn't more been done to tackle it?

This year, however, the Delhi government announced its Winter Action Plan months before the worst of the smog arrived. The plan is in place from 1 November to 28 February, covering the months when pollution usually spikes.

Experts have called this a step in the right direction, noting that in previous years measures were often rolled out only after the air quality got too bad to ignore. However, they say this by itself won't be enough, calling for more holistic, long-lasting measures.

Just days after the plan came into effect, the city is slipping back into a depressingly familiar pattern .

This week, a grey haze hangs over Delhi, along with a distinct smoky smell that residents unwillingly recognise. People complain of irritation in their eyes and difficulty breathing, and coughs and sneezes are heard everywhere.

For those who can afford them, air purifiers have become a household necessity. Outdoors, people wear masks or cover their faces with cloth, trying to protect themselves from the worst of the pollution.

Tackling pollution was among the promises made by the governing Bharatiya Janata Party during its election campaign last year. Its winter action plan is now a major test of that pledge.

The plan restricts the entry of older, more polluting vehicles registered outside Delhi and denies fuel to vehicles without a certificate which shows they meet emission standards. Demolitions and outdoor construction work that generate dust have been temporarily banned.

Private vehicle use is being discouraged - the government has asked offices to allow half of their employees to work from home, introduced staggered office timings for its staff and doubled parking charges. It says it will also strengthen pollution monitoring and enforcement and promote public transport and electric vehicles.

These measures are separate from the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap), which is overseen by the federal Commission for Air Quality Management.

Grap introduces restrictions in stages, with stricter measures kicking in as pollution levels rise. This week, its second stage is in force, restricting the use of diesel generators and burning of coal and firewood.

Experts say on paper, these actions collectively provide a roadmap for responding to rising pollution levels but their success ultimately depends on enforcement.

"There are a lot of positive changes as far as planning is concerned, but when it comes to execution, we probably still stand at the same level," says Parthaa Bosu, strategic adviser at the Environmental Defense Fund, a non-profit group focused on delivering climate solutions.

"If we want to reduce pollution, we need to set targets for every sector - including power generation, industry and transport - not just vehicle entry, construction and stubble burning," says Manoj Kumar, an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

"We know how much each sector and each state contributes to pollution. We can set targets to reduce emissions from each of them over the next five years."

Bosu points out that an issue which does not get enough attention is secondary pollutants - when gases in the air react with sunlight, water vapour and other substances to form harmful particles that contribute to pollution.

"Pollution is not just caused by biomass burning or vehicles," he says. "Dust being stirred up from the ground, coal and fly ash, materials burned at brick kilns and the large-scale burning of urban waste are also contributing to the problem. And much of this is still not being stopped."

Delhi's pollution problem is also affected by what happens outside the city . Pollutants travel into Delhi from neighbouring states and other parts of northern India, worsening the situation, Bosu explains.

This means that measures taken by Delhi can achieve only so much. Tackling the problem requires neighbouring states and the wider northern region to work together, he adds.

'I panic every time she coughs' - Delhi's toxic air is making its children sick

Why India caps pollution reading at 500 when the air is far more toxic

Living in Delhi smog is like watching a dystopian film again and again

In the meantime, pollution is harming people's health every day.

During winter, government monitoring stations in Delhi frequently record Air Quality Index (AQI) readings above 300, classified as "very poor".

On particularly bad days, readings can reach 500, the highest point on India's scale. That does not mean pollution cannot rise further, only that domestic trackers do not record it. International trackers such as Swiss-based IQAir have recorded readings close to 1,000 on some days.

The World Health Organization recommends average PM2.5 levels over 24 hours should not exceed 15 micrograms per cubic metre. In Delhi, levels are often at more than 25 times that limit during pollution season.

Dr Manoj Goel, pulmonology unit head at Fortis Memorial Research Institute near Delhi, says these tiny particles "can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, triggering inflammation and affecting multiple organs".

Even short-term exposure can cause throat irritation, coughing, wheezing and breathlessness. It can also worsen existing heart and lung conditions.

A 2025 report , external by the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago estimated that air pollution could reduce life expectancy in Delhi by up to 8.2 years.

For residents, the challenge is not just limited to breathing. The restrictions also disrupt everyday life.

Delhi is closely connected to its satellite towns, Noida and Gurugram, with thousands of people travelling between them every day for work. Long queues form at the city's borders as vehicles are stopped and checked, leaving commuters stuck in traffic for hours.

While the new rules offer some hope, frustration is growing.

Protests, political arguments and court interventions have become part of the annual cycle. But despite public pressure and government measures, the pollution returns every winter.

Rana keeps her windows closed and curtains drawn, and has added more indoor plants.

The arrival of another winter fills her family with dread, but unlike many others , they are not planning to move out of Delhi.

"I would have left the city long ago had there been an option, but my son has his school, my husband and I have our jobs as well, which makes it practically impossible," she says.

"What option do we have? It is unfair but we will have to live with it."

items.title: Cuban: Facebook knowingly runs AI deepfake scam ads; docs say $16B fraud revenue
items.summary: Article URL: https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/mark-cuban-says-facebook-knowingly-213000020.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50385870 Points: 319 # Comments: 153
items.content:
Mark Cuban keeps getting emails about a $294 diabetes cure he has never sold.

"Every single week I get emails from little old men and ladies saying, 'Will my cure for diabetes work?' or 'I just ordered your cure for diabetes for $294,'" the 68-year-old billionaire investor said on an August episode of Pivot , the podcast hosted by Kara Swisher and Scott Galloway.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

Those ads are deepfakes built with an AI copy of his face and voice, Cuban said, and Meta (NASDAQ:META) runs them anyway. "Facebook knows the little old ladies are getting ripped off," he said. He called the platform "the worst of the worst."

Cuban said some of the ads even include a disclaimer admitting the person on screen is AI-generated and the clip is meant as entertainment. By the time anyone gets to it, he argued, the pitch has already worked. "And to Facebook, that's good enough," he said.

"The point is, that defines the culture of the organization," Cuban said. A company that lets scammers go after people's grandparents, he argued, has shown what it will tolerate at every level.

Cuban does run a drug company — he co-founded Cost Plus Drugs , an online pharmacy that sells low-cost generic medications.

On Nov. 6, 2025, Reuters reported on internal Meta documents showing the company expected roughly $16 billion, or about 10% of its 2024 revenue, to flow in from ads pushing scams and prohibited products. By Meta's own internal count, users across its apps were seeing some 15 billion "higher risk" ads a day — the ones with obvious markers of fraud. One late 2024 document put that category's value at about $7 billion a year.

In a May 2025 presentation, Meta's own safety staff estimated the company's platforms play a part in a third of the scams that succeed in the U.S. Before Meta bans an advertiser, its automated systems must peg the account as at least 95% likely to be running a scam, the documents say . Below that threshold, the suspected scammer simply pays more per ad and stays live.

Meta spokesman Andy Stone told Reuters the documents "present a selective view that distorts Meta's approach to fraud and scams," and called the company's 10% estimate "rough and overly-inclusive." Complaints from users about scam ads had fallen 58% over the prior 18 months, he said at the time, and the company pulled down more than 134 million scam ads in 2025. The same documents note the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Meta over advertising tied to financial fraud.

items.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
items.summary: California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US.
items.content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, changing them instead to life in prison.

"We can now let these offenders die in obscurity while we forever remember and honour the victims," he said in a letter.

The decision to spare death row inmates is largely symbolic in a state that has not executed an inmate since 2006, though experts say it could save millions of dollars in court costs each year. Only 13 inmates have been executed since voters reinstated the death penalty in 1978.

The decision comes as Newsom, the Democratic leader of the most populous US state, has been discussed as a possible 2028 contender for president.

Newsom, who is term limited, is winding down his final months in office. Fellow Democrat Xavier Becerra is projected to take over after the midterm elections on Tuesday.

Newsom explained in his letter that he is exercising his constitutional clemency authority to commute the sentences to life without the possibility of parole.

"After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom said. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values, undermines the foundations of our legal system and diminishes each of us".

California has historically had the largest population of death row inmates. Newsom had previously ordered a halt to the death penalty in the state in 2019.

Describing his decision as a difficult but "righteous action", Newsom said that although many Californians feel that those who commit brutal crimes deserve to die, he has concluded that "the state cannot morally kill them".

He said that by every measure, California's system for administering the death penalty "is a failure", and that it has not and cannot be fairly applied, resulting in the conviction of innocent people.

Life without the possibility of parole is the most severe punishment he can lawfully impose and that the state can ethically enforce, he said.

He acknowledged that his clemency action will anger and hurt some Californians and said that it will "always weigh heavily on me".

"As governor, I alone bear responsibility for this decision and its impact, just as I alone would bear responsibility for each execution," he wrote.

"For this reason, I am compelled to follow my conscience and, as authorised by our Constitution, take this action for the welfare of the State of California."

Because individual states have the power to prosecute crimes and order executions, much of the power lies with state governors.

Bernard E Harcourt, a law and civil liberties professor at Columbia University, told the BBC that it is not unprecedented for a potential presidential candidate to come out as an abolitionist in the run up to elections - despite the overall popularity of the death penalty in the US.

He noted that François Mitterrand did precisely that in his presidential campaign in France in 1981, taking "the higher ethical ground and was rewarded by the public for that".

"I detect a very similar ethical positioning in Governor Newsom's statements about the commutations. And here too, it may well be something that the voters respect," he said.

Newsom's decision comes after the high-profile botched execution of a woman in Tennessee in late September and while executions have been on the rise in the US. There are three executions scheduled for Thursday in Indiana, Florida and Alabama.

At least four of seven judges on the California Supreme Court will have to sign off on the commutations, CalMatters reported.

It is unclear how Newsom's decision will affect condemned inmates like Keith Doolin, 53, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for murdering two sex workers, Inez Espinoza and Peggy Tucker, and shooting four others. He maintains his innocence.

Doolin lived on death row at San Quentin for decades, until he was moved to another prison in 2025 when the governor announced the state would reform the prison for all but those on death row .

Doolin's mother, Donna Larsen, told the BBC that the news of Newsom's commutations - which includes Doolin - brought mixed emotions.

"At least the execution chamber will not be reconstructed, and no more killing by the people of the state of California," she said.

Anthony D Romero, the executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union, applauded Newsom's action.

"These commutations reflect what justice demands: an end to a racist, error-prone, and inhumane punishment that has burdened California for far too long," Romero said.

"By taking this step, Gov. Newsom has affirmed that the death penalty has no place in California and he showed real courage by confronting racialised injustice head-on."

Nathan Hochman, the top prosecutor in Los Angeles County, said that while Newsom has the power to commute sentences, only state legislature or voters can eliminate the death penalty.

"Californians have been asked on two separate ballot initiatives to abolish the death penalty and both times they have chosen to keep it for the most serious crimes," Hochman said in a statement.

On the federal level, President Donald Trump, a long-time supporter of the death penalty, has described capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

In 2020, during his first term, he ended a nearly two-decade moratorium on the federal death penalty, by ordering 13 executions over a six-month period.

While the moratorium returned under President Biden, on the first day of Trump's second term in 2025, he signed an executive order that re-instated the death penalty.

No federal executions have been carried out since he signed it, however. In the US, both the federal government and local states authorities can order executions.

The death penalty is legal in 27 states, but has been abolished in 23 states and Washington DC, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, a national non-profit.

California, which primarily uses lethal injection for executions, used to house male death row prisoners in San Quentin State Prison north of San Francisco, and female inmates in the Central California Women's Facility in the Central Valley.

But a 2016 ballot measure allowed for their transfer to other facilities that provide a necessary level of security, according to the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation.

items.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
items.summary: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.
items.content:
Nigeria's Federal High Court has sacked the leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) party - and also ruled that the nomination of its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, is invalid.

A statement from the ADC said the ruling was another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition.

Presidential elections are scheduled to take place on 16 January when President Bola Tinubu's main challengers are again expected to be Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi.

Several high-profile politicians joined the ADC in 2025 - disillusioned by the factional infighting in the once powerful Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Among them were Abubakar - who had served as vice-president between 1999 and 2007 when the PDP was in power - and former Senate president David Mark.

As accommodations were made for the line-up of political heavyweights, Mark took over as its interim chairman.

But Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former ADC national deputy chairman, argued before the court that this was not lawful as Mark and others had not been elected at a national convention.

Instead, he said, he himself should have taken over the party's leadership following the resignation of the ADC's former chairman in 2025.

This is not first time the Federal High Court in the capital, Abuja, has ruled on the leadership of the party.

In July, judge Musa Liman said Mark had been chosen in accordance with the country's laws and the party's constitution - in a case brought by another former ADC member.

Abubakar said the latest case raised serious legal concerns: "Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute?"

In a statement, the ADC added that Thursday's judgement by Justice Peter Lifu was aimed at stifling the opposition momentum and "was a calculated attempt to weaken the ADC and frustrate" Abubakar's candidacy.

The ADC says it will challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal.

In a statement on X, Abubakar, 79, said it showed the "panic was real" by those who felt threatened by his candidacy , external .

He said the timing of the judgment was telling as it came "barely a day after a mammoth crowd turned out in Sokoto [northern Nigeria] to welcome him" at the launch of his campaign.

"The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning."

Political parties in Nigeria have increasingly been taking internal issues to court.

But as it stands, the electoral commission has issued its final list of candidates , external - and Abubakar is on the ticket for the ADC with former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as his running mate.

The ADC is seen as the most powerful opposition to President Tinubu. Many influential politicians opposed to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) have already defected to the party.

The legal saga could complicate things - it may cause uncertainty for hundreds of ADC candidates as well as raise questions over who has the authority to represent them.

But Abubakar, who is running for the presidency for a seventh time, is confident the matter will be resolved and called on his supporters not to be distracted.

"Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis. We urge our supporters to remain resolute, take our message from house to house and door to door, and stay peaceful and focused," the 79-year-old said.

Peter Obi - the other main presidential candidate, who is on the ballot for a second time - has said he is shocked by Thursday's high court ruling.

He released a statement on X with the heading , external : "Do not undermine democracy".

The 65-year-old went on to say: "My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty.

Obi had briefly joined the ADC before leaving earlier this year to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) - in part because of the legal challenges within the ADC.

"The sustenance of democracy in Nigeria, in the midst of encroaching military rule in West Africa, should strengthen our resolve to protect opposition politics and not stamp out opposition parties," he said.

The NDC's candidate said that, as president, he would ensure that the existence of opposition parties would be respected.

"This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive."

items.title: Al via il nuovo Quotidiano Nazionale, 'patto con i lettori: liberi di darci torto'
items.summary: Da La Russa a Meloni per l'evento a Roma. Del Vecchio: "Punto sull'editoria"
items.content:
Parte da oggi l'avventura del nuovo Quotidiano Nazionale e all'evento di presentazione alla Galleria di Arte Moderna a Roma l'editore Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio assicura che intende puntare sempre più sul settore. "Assolutamente sì", risponde ai cronisti che gli chiedono se intende fare nuovi investimenti, prima di parlare di un "grande inizio". All'evento, oltre all'erede del fondatore di Luxottica che è arrivato con la figlia Bianca in braccio, tanti esponenti politici e istituzionali, dal presidente del Senato Ignazio La Russa alla premier Giorgia Meloni con la sorella Arianna, fino ai ministri Matteo Salvini, Matteo Piantedosi e Antonio Tajani ea al sottosegretario all'Editoria Alberto Barachini. Presenti anche la sottosegretaria alla Cultura Lucia Borgonzoni. "Quando un giornale si rinnova e cresce, cresce la democrazia", ha detto quest'ultimo. Per l'opposizione sono intervenuti Elly Schlein, Giuseppe Conte, Angelo Bonelli e Matteo Renzi. Il sindaco di Roma Roberto Gualtieri si è detto felice per la scelta della capitale come sede. Tra gli altri anche il presidente dell'Agcom Giacomo Lasorella, il presidente della Fieg Andrea Riffeser Monti, Bruno Vespa e Fedez, vicino a Del Vecchio ormai da alcuni mesi, e Giovanni Malagò.

Durante l'evento Del Vecchio, l'amministratore delegato Gabriele Benedetto, il direttore editoriale Mario Orfeo e la direttrice Agnese Pini hanno tracciato i contorni del progetto editoriale. "Cominciamo oggi perché ogni inizio è anche una dichiarazione d'intenti. Il 5 novembre 2026 è all'indomani delle Midterm americane, che in altri tempi avremmo documentato come un naturale tagliando di metà mandato della più grande democrazia occidentale, ma che oggi segnano il punto d'avvio dell'anno elettorale che verrà", ha scritto oggi Pini nel suo editoriale dal titolo "Un giornale nuovo e un patto con gli elettori. Liberi di darci torto". Nella prima pagina una sola grande foto con Donald Trump sotto un cielo plumbeo, attorniato dai giornalisti, e il titolo di apertura "L'America scarica Trump. È guerra alla Casa Bianca". A contornarla i richiami degli articoli delle pagine interne con gli interventi del filosofo Luciano Floridi, dello scrittore Edoardo Nesi e del presidente della Biennale di Venezia Pietrangelo Buttafuoco e un fumetto di Gipi. In taglio basso l'editoriale sulle elezioni di Midterm di Mattia Feltri. Il quotidiano ospita anche il pensiero della premier Giorgia Meloni sul rapporto con gli Stati Uniti. "Al nuovo Qn hanno deciso di partecipare alcune fra le menti più brillanti del nostro tempo e del nostro Paese", ha spiegato ancora Pini nel suo editoriale. "Nell'epoca delle verità imposte, riteniamo più credibile il dubbio - ha sottolineato -. L'indipendenza di un giornale si riconosce soprattutto perché decide di pubblicare anche quando quel fatto smentisce le sue convinzioni".
